validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real and correctly classified. This is FERC Docket CP18-103-000, 'Rockies Express Pipeline LLC's Cheyenne Hub Enhancement Project' — six new 5,350 hp reciprocating compressor units (32,100 hp total) plus bi-directional modifications to the existing CIG and Trailblazer interconnect meter stations, all at REX's existing Cheyenne Compressor Station in Weld County, Colorado (FERC order, issued 2019-09-20). Certificate authorized by FERC 2019-09-20 (168 FERC P 61,180); construction confirmed to have commenced 2019-10-17 per REX's own report to FERC, quoted in a 2021-01-11 PHMSA enforcement warning letter to REX's CEO (a federal document independent of both FERC and the applicant, naming the project explicitly and confirming it as a real, built facility -- PHMSA physically inspected the compressor station Feb-Dec 2020). Commercial service began 2020-06-26 per Tallgrass's own press release and independently reported by World Pipelines (2020-06-29, 'Cheyenne Connector and Rockies Express pipelines back in service'). Correctly classified as gas transmission (FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas company under the NGA) and correctly NOT a duplicate of P0359 Cheyenne Connector -- that is a separate, physically distinct ~70-mile gathering-to-transmission lateral built by a different joint venture (Tallgrass/DCP/Anadarko/WGP) that DELIVERS INTO this project's Cheyenne Hub facilities; the two projects were filed the same day (2018-03-05) in companion FERC dockets (CP18-102 for Cheyenne Connector, CP18-103 for this project) and are frequently discussed together in press, which is why they are easy to conflate but are not the same pipeline. DUPLICATE check against the 46-row roster: no other row references the Cheyenne Hub Enhancement Project; not a duplicate of P0246 (REX Main Line, a different segment/scope) or of P0359. Of the 30 URLs harvested from this row's gem.wiki page, none specifically cover the Cheyenne Hub Enhancement Project (2018-2020) -- the harvested pool is dominated by REX's 2007-2009 original construction and 2016-2017 ownership-transaction coverage. All data below therefore came from open-web/FERC-docket research, not the harvested pool. Two harvested citations (Hart Energy 2016 stake-sale article, and a 2016 BusinessWire release) were attempted directly and failed (Hart Energy: HTTP 403 bot-wall via curl w/ browser UA; BusinessWire: repeated ReadTimeout on retry) -- both were consequently NOT used; the same facts were instead confirmed from SEC filings (see Owner finding).

validity.recommendation: Update Owner1%/Owner2/Owner2% -- Phillips 66 sold its 25% non-operated equity interest in Rockies Express Pipeline LLC to a Tallgrass Energy subsidiary in 2024; Tallgrass now owns 100%.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's recorded 75%/25% Tallgrass/Phillips 66 split was correct as of LastUpdated (2023-08-29) -- see the Owner fill below for two independent, dated sources confirming that split. But it is now STALE: Phillips 66 agreed to sell its full 25% non-operated interest in REX to a Tallgrass Energy LP subsidiary for an enterprise value of ~$1.275-1.28bn, closing in 2024, leaving Tallgrass owning 100% of REX. Confirmed independently by Oil & Gas Journal ('Tallgrass Energy to gain full ownership of REX in deal with Phillips 66') and NS Energy Business ('Phillips 66 sells Rockies Express Pipeline stake to Tallgrass Energy') -- two independent trade-press origins, both 2024. This is a real-world ownership change the sheet has not yet caught up to; flagging rather than silently overwriting since it postdates the row's own LastUpdated and a researcher should confirm the exact 2024 closing date before editing Owner2/Owner2%.

validity.recommendation: Verify EndState/Province -- this project's entire physical scope (compressor station modification) sits in Weld County, Colorado; 'Illinois' does not match either the project's physical location or REX's actual system terminus (Clarington, Ohio). Consider Ohio (matching sibling row P0246, the REX Main Line) or Colorado (matching the project's actual footprint), pending a researcher call on which convention this row should follow.
validity.researcher_notes: StartState/Province=Colorado is well-supported (the Cheyenne Compressor Station enhancement is entirely within Weld County, Colorado -- FERC order CP18-103-000; Tallgrass press release: 'the REX Cheyenne Hub, positioned just south of the Wyoming border ... in southern Weld County, Colorado'). EndState/Province=Illinois is NOT supported by any source found and is inconsistent with the roster: sibling row P0246 (REX Main Line, same system) records EndState=Ohio, and Wikipedia's infobox for Rockies Express Pipeline gives the system route as 'Meeker, Colorado' to 'Clarington, Ohio', passing through Wyoming, Nebraska, Kansas, Missouri, Illinois, Indiana -- i.e. Illinois is a PASS-THROUGH state on the REX system, not its terminus. The FERC order does list Illinois among the states where REX holds certificated service ('transportation services in Colorado, Wyoming, Nebraska, Kansas, Missouri, Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio'), so Illinois is not fabricated, but it is not this project's or the system's terminus. I did not force a correction because this is a compression-only, single-county project and a researcher should decide whether a sourced segment-level End should be the system terminus (Ohio, matching P0246) or the project's own footprint (Colorado, since no gas leaves Colorado as part of THIS specific facility upgrade) -- see cross_row_leads for the related P0246 length/route finding.

validity.recommendation: Correct SegmentCost from $185,000,000 to the FERC-certificated project cost estimate of $132,805,200 (Docket CP18-103-000), or find a primary source that supports $185M before keeping it.
validity.researcher_notes: MATERIAL DISAGREEMENT. The FERC order for this exact project (CP18-103-000, the Cheyenne Hub Enhancement Project) states: 'Rockies Express estimates the total cost of the Cheyenne Hub Enhancement Project to be $132,805,200.' That is ~$52.2M (28%) below the sheet's recorded $185,000,000. I could not find any primary source stating $185M. The only other place I found that figure was cgaa.org ('Rockies Express Pipeline Expansion Increases Energy Capacity'), an SEO/content-aggregator site whose figures for this project (capacity, cost, in-service date) match GEM's own recorded values exactly, including the $185M -- that is much more consistent with cgaa.org having scraped/paraphrased GEM's wiki than with it being an independent corroboration, so I did not count it and did not cite it. I did not find a second primary source restating $132,805,200 either (searched Reuters, S&P Global, NGI, Hart Energy, RBN Energy -- RBN Energy's relevant piece 403'd; Hart Energy 403'd; none of the harvested wiki citations cover this project) -- tier is medium rather than high because only one primary source states a specific number, but that source (the FERC certificate order itself, which quotes the applicant's own cost estimate as adopted in the Commission's findings) is about as authoritative as a pre-construction cost estimate gets, and it directly and specifically contradicts the recorded value.

cross_row_leads.facts: Wikipedia's infobox for the whole Rockies Express Pipeline system gives length 1,679 miles (2,702 km), diameter 36-42 in (primarily 42 in), max capacity 3.6 Bcf/d, MAOP 1,480 psi, route Meeker, Colorado -> Clarington, Ohio via Wyoming, Nebraska, Kansas, Missouri, Illinois, Indiana. P0246 (REX Main Line, this roster) is recorded at LengthKnown=1685.0 km -- suspiciously close to 1,679 MILES (not km); this looks like the same mile/km mixup this batch's brief warned about (a value in miles relabeled as km). Worth a direct check against the FERC docket/EIA figures for P0246 rather than assuming Wikipedia is right, but the near-exact match to the mile figure is a strong signal. Also: P0246's recorded Capacity=4050 MMcf/d vs Wikipedia's 'max 3.6 Bcf/d' -- not necessarily wrong (GEM's figure may be a post-expansion cumulative total including Cheyenne Hub and other add-ons that predate Wikipedia's cited figure), but worth a look. Route confirms Illinois is a PASS-THROUGH state on the REX system, not the terminus (Ohio is) -- relevant to this row's (P2517) own EndState/Province=Illinois concern, and confirms P0246's own EndState=Ohio is correct.
